case: Mariner Calibration Services: original finite-return-fade model
provenance: Original fictional teaching assumptions, not observed company or market data. Prepared 2026-10-08.
period: one year; all free cash flow and reinvestment at year-end
valuation_date: date 0, immediately after any date-0 distributions
maintained_assumptions: NOPAT in year t equals the supplied ROIC times beginning-year operating capital; that ROIC applies to all capital then productive.
Net reinvestment at end t becomes productive in t+1; capital has no acquisition, currency, impairment, revaluation or other noncash movement.
Net PPE is always 80 percent of operating capital; operating NWC is 20 percent and excludes excess cash, debt and interest.
Depreciation is 5 percent of opening net PPE; capex replaces that book consumption and finances the PPE share of net investment. This is a case policy, not an empirical maintenance estimate.

Cash operating costs, required reinvestment and tax are feasible under the supplied annual aggregate model. Tax deductions match book depreciation and all operating tax is paid; no deferred tax or unusable loss exists.
Return on all opening capital reaches the stable return in the final explicit year; that year's reinvestment already uses stable growth divided by stable ROIC.
Stable growth is nonnegative, below the supplied operating discount rate, and no greater than stable ROIC; reinvestment is internally financed from positive NOPAT in this bounded model.
Discount rates are hypothetical appropriate rates for these operating cash claims under the maintained risk and financing convention; the model does not estimate them or add another tax shield.
The equity bridge uses separately supplied date-0 market claim values. It does not model debt repayment or default; negative residual equity is outside its non-distress scope.
No interim cash calendar, uncertainty probabilities, market-comparable evidence, calibration or perpetual competitive advantage is inferred from arithmetic.
